stories.title: Rhino siblings celebrate first birthday with cake
summary: Markus and Mo weighed about 70kg (11st) at birth, and now weigh about 500kg (78st) each.

stories.title: 'Fascinating' rare beetle found in Wales again after 60 years
summary: It was feared The Short-Necked Oil Beetle had become extinct in Wales after recent surveys

stories.title: Oil tank vandalism results in waterfowl park 'nightmare'
summary: The popular attraction in County Down has been forced to close while efforts continue to remove oil from the pond.

stories.title: 'Rok' solid recognition for Slovenian space scientist
summary: Two men from the Armagh Planetarium and Observatory have had asteroids named in their honour in recognition of their work.

stories.title: Rare damselfly spotted by restored chalk river
summary: The Herts and Middlesex Trust says it is "thrilled" the new wetlands are helping species thrive.

stories.title: Scientists say a forgotten particle may explain why the universe exists
summary: A mysterious particle overlooked for decades may hold the key to why matter survived the Big Bang, allowing stars, planets, and life to exist.
Scientists believe this forgotten neutrino reshaped the early universe and may have left detectable gravitational wave signals that could help unlock the cosmos’s deepest mysteries.

stories.title: Scientists discover the hidden “muscles” trees use to straighten themselves
summary: Scientists have discovered that trees can sense their own shape and straighten their trunks using specialized wood that acts like opposing muscles.
This remarkable ability helps trees maintain their posture and could lead to stronger forests, better timber, and more resilient crops.

stories.title: Bute House protested by environmental campaigners
summary: A Halloween-themed protest against fossil fuels has targeted the first minister's residence in Edinburgh.

stories.title: A mysterious 4,000-year-old wall is rewriting North Africa’s history
summary: A remarkable 4,000-year-old defensive structure discovered in Morocco is rewriting what scientists thought they knew about ancient North African civilizations.
The massive fortifications reveal unexpectedly sophisticated prehistoric societies and suggest that the region played a much greater role in Mediterranean history than previously recognized.

stories.title: Scientists discover metals that defy the deep freeze at -424°F
summary: Scientists have discovered a surprising mechanism that allows certain metals to resist cracking at temperatures as low as -253°C (-424°F), when similar materials typically become dangerously brittle.
Instead of breaking, two experimental alloys reorganize their internal structures, creating new ways to absorb stress and remain flexible.

stories.title: 75,000-year-old Neanderthal may have been killed by a spear aimed at the heart
summary: A Neanderthal who died 75,000 years ago may have been killed by a wooden spear deliberately aimed at the heart, revealing rare evidence of prehistoric violence.
A circular hole in the shoulder blade suggests the weapon pierced the chest and caused a rapidly fatal injury.
Surprisingly, the same individual had survived an earlier devastating facial injury, suggesting other Neanderthals provided care and support.

stories.title: Scientists discover a bacterial defense so strange they thought it was broken
summary: Scientists have discovered a bizarre bacterial defense system that works almost completely backward from anything seen before.

Unlike typical bacterial immune systems that keep a deadly toxin under control until a virus attacks, this unusual mechanism waits until an infection begins before producing the DNA that switches on its lethal weapon.
The infected bacterium then destroys itself, preventing the virus from multiplying and spreading to neighboring cells.

stories.title: Rewilding project aims to restore peatland
summary: Cumbria Wildlife Trust starts work repairing damage to Skiddaw Forest's peatland.

stories.title: A surprising vitamin A discovery is changing what scientists know about vision
summary: Scientists at Johns Hopkins University have uncovered a surprising process that helps humans develop sharp vision before birth, challenging decades of assumptions about how the eye forms.

Using miniature human retinas grown in the lab, researchers discovered that a vitamin A derivative and thyroid hormones work together to shape the foveola, the tiny region at the center of the retina responsible for our sharpest vision.

stories.title: Scientists smash oxygen nuclei to recreate matter from the Big Bang
summary: Scientists have recreated a primordial state of matter from the dawn of the universe by colliding oxygen nuclei at nearly the speed of light.
The surprising results show that this exotic substance can form in smaller, lower-energy collisions than previously demonstrated, challenging the known boundaries of early-universe physics.

stories.title: A simple blood test could reveal Alzheimer’s risk 10 years before symptoms
summary: A major international study found that a simple blood test could help predict Alzheimer’s-related cognitive decline years before symptoms appear, with the highest-risk individuals facing a 38% chance of impairment within five years and an estimated 78% chance within 10 years.
Scientists believe the discovery could pave the way for earlier intervention and future treatments designed to prevent Alzheimer’s before memory problems begin.

stories.title: UK could see 10 days without rain after 'wettest week in two years'
summary: With high pressure developing across the UK, the start of November is looking very settled with no significant rain in the forecast.
